question: Q5 (spend per visit/cup)
trigger_or_metric: share of Gen Z coffee drinkers spending under Rp10,000 per cup (bought or made)
population: Indonesian Gen Z, national online panel (Jakpat)
proxy_note: Cup spend, not café ticket; buy or home-made combined; price ceiling signal
snippet: a JakPat survey reveals that the majority (48%) of Indonesian Gen Z respondents spend less than Rp10,000 on buying or making a cup of coffee
notes: Published 2025-01-07 per search summary; tier 3 via Databoks; 'majority' wording is the republisher's, 48% is not a majority; base n=1,155 is the survey total, base for the 48% not confirmed; verifier must open; V-E: 48%, fieldwork and n=1,155 confirmed (Databoks 2025-01-07, Goodstats); base for the 48% still unconfirmed (chart paywalled); 48% is a plurality, not a majority. Audit: single-outlet reliance.

notes: Published 2025-07-17 per search summary; tier 3 (Katadata Insight Center and tSurvey via Databoks); non-probability sample; weak; V-E: CONFLICT: a second Databoks article on the same survey gives 64% for dining and base 266 or 268 depending on the article. Non-probability sample.

question: Q6 (daypart)
trigger_or_metric: share of frequent diners usually eating out for dinner
unit: % of frequent diners (question wording not confirmed)
population: Frequent diners, online Jakpat app, 8 urban cities on Java (Jakarta not separated)
proxy_note: Java urban proxy; age 15-25 vs target 25-39
snippet: the majority of young Indonesians tend to eat out for lunch and dinner, at 23% and 41% respectively
notes: V-E: fieldwork 2-7 Sep 2025 confirmed, so publication is after the cutoff; exact page date not seen (inferred 2025-10-31). Base CONFLICT: 955 total, 769 frequent diners (Databoks); a Jakpat write-up says 995. Both Databoks pieces and Jakpat give dinner 41%. Tier 3.

question: Q6 (daypart)
trigger_or_metric: share of frequent diners usually eating out for lunch
unit: % of frequent diners (question wording not confirmed)
population: Frequent diners, online Jakpat app, 8 urban cities on Java (Jakarta not separated)
proxy_note: Java urban proxy; age 15-25 vs target 25-39; value conflicts with a second Databoks piece (37%, undated, excluded)
snippet: the majority of young Indonesians tend to eat out for lunch and dinner, at 23% and 41% respectively
notes: V-E correction: value 37% (Jakpat Insight and a second source; dinner 41%, lunch 37%). The Databoks text prints 23%, most likely a typo. H6 test: lunch 37% vs dinner 41%.
